Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 10%, stress 60%, tail 30%.

todaysEvents.delta: AP reported the ministers discussed a joint temporary navigational corridor and mine-clearance project, while Reuters said talks restarted under mounting economic pressure (AP/Reuters, Aug 25-26).
AP reported an oil tanker was disabled in an attack off Oman, underscoring ongoing hazards while the strait remains largely shut (AP, Aug 25).
Brent fell to $85.74, down 8.57%, while TTF rose 1.27% to 66.13 EUR/MWh as reopening hopes met continued LNG supply risk (Yahoo Finance, Aug 26; TTF Aug 25).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman advance a temporary corridor and mine-clearance framework; a signed, monitored reopening restores traffic and lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The corridor remains provisional and traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and residual mine and attack risk; Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: A failed framework, further tanker attack or sanctions retaliation could close the southern lane again and spill into Bab el-Mandeb; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.

Working range $75-85 base (signed workable deal); $78-95 stress (conditional routing); $105-135+ tail (renewed closure).
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters September-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $21.22/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Aug 14), carried on Aug 26. Qatar force majeure is carried through mid-September from the Reuters Jul 23 notice; the reported mid-October extension remains unconfirmed.
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> 63.58/MWh (Jul 24, MacroMicro) -> 66.13 EUR/MWh (Aug 25, Yahoo Finance TTF=F; +1.27%) as Iran-Oman corridor talks advanced but the framework remained provisional and Qatar LNG force majeure persisted. The marker remains elevated versus the pre-crisis baseline while route and supply risks remain unresolved.
